subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: For non-group, not-from-me iMessage DMs where sender normalizes to destination_caller_id but peer recovery is ambiguous or impossible, should OpenClaw drop before access control or continue with the original sender path?
rationale: That choice decides whether an ambiguous local-sender payload can reach allowlist, pairing, routing, and reply decisions; code review cannot infer the intended security boundary from the current PR alone.

options.title: Fail Closed On Ambiguous Repair
options.body: Drop unrecoverable local-sender DM payloads before access control and cover that invariant with focused tests.

options.title: Repair Only Unique Peer Cases
options.body: Accept the current fallback behavior for ambiguous payloads while only repairing payloads with a canonical, unique peer candidate.

options.title: Pause For Separate Root Cause
options.body: If the author's remaining failure is not this race, pause or close this branch and track the narrower iMessage issue separately.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed On Ambiguous Repair
recommendation.body: Drop unrecoverable local-sender DM payloads before access control and cover that invariant with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent iMessage self-chat and echo-path work plus related PR approvals make them the best available routing candidate for this identity-boundary choice.
